title: Laredo District 3 race: water losses, flooding and Highway 359 traffic top candidates' pitches
excerpt: Incumbent Melissa Cigarroa and challenger Clarissa “Claire” Cardenas outlined their District 3 priorities as early voting continues through Oct. 30, KGNS reported; challenger Michelle “Mimi” Winterroth declined an interview.
content:
Incumbent Melissa Cigarroa and challenger Clarissa “Claire” Cardenas outlined their priorities for Laredo City Council District 3 as early voting continues through October 30, KGNS reported October 28. A third candidate, Michelle “Mimi” Winterroth, declined an interview, according to KGNS.

The issues the candidates named were flooding, aging water lines, and Highway 359 traffic. Cigarroa, who has lived in District 3 for more than 30 years, cited 4 to 6 million gallons of water lost daily through leaks and said the district needs a Highway 359 relief route. She said, in part: “we lose between 4 to 6 million gallons of water a day just through leaks, leaky pipes.”

Cardenas, who has lived in District 3 for about five years, called traffic the district's biggest local issue, according to KGNS.

What to watch next: the final days of early voting through October 30, and Election Day on November 3, when District 3 voters choose among Cigarroa, Cardenas and Winterroth.

Sources:

  • KGNS, “District 3 candidates outline priorities as early voting continues,” October 28, 2026
